question.text: Three identical particle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> each are placed in a straight line with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>13</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The gravitational force on a fourth particle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> of the same mass is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi></math>, when placed at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>13</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> from the particle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> on the perpendicular bisector of the line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mi>C</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi></math> will be approximately

solution.text:
Given here, m=100 kg

Gravitational force, FAP=Gm21322,

FBP=Gm2132 and FCP=Gm21322

Net gravitational force, 

Fnet=FBP+FAPcos45°+FCPcos45°

 =G×1041321+12

F≃100G
